Guernsey Metals & Mining Industry Posts Steady Growth in First Quarter

The metals and mining sector in Guernsey recorded steady growth in the first quarter of 2024, according to newly released figures from the Channel Islands Mining Association (CIMA). The data indicates that the industry maintained its positive momentum, supported by stable global demand and continued investment in exploration and processing capacity.

Aggregate mining output reached 1.22 million metric tonnes, a 3.1% increase compared to the same period in 2023. The sector’s overall revenue climbed to £168 million, up from £162 million a year earlier. Prices for key exports, including iron ore and non-ferrous metals, remained resilient despite fluctuations in broader commodity markets.

“We’re seeing consistent, measured growth across the board,” said Jean-Paul Renard, CIMA’s chair. “Our members have benefited from strong relationships with European buyers, and infrastructure investments made over the past two years are now bearing fruit in terms of efficiency and output.”

Guernsey’s largest operator, Atlantic Quarry Holdings, reported a 4% rise in quarterly production. “We are pleased with our performance, which reflects both operational improvements and a favourable market environment,” said Managing Director Lucy Forester. “Our focus on sustainable mining practices continues to resonate with our customers.”

Employment in the sector remained steady, with around 700 people directly employed and more than 300 jobs supported indirectly through supply chains and service providers. The Guernsey Mining Workers Union welcomed the positive results. Union spokesperson Peter Leclerc commented, “Stability in employment and safety standards is good news for our members and the island as a whole.”

Analysts expect the industry to remain on a stable footing for the coming quarters, given ongoing infrastructure upgrades at the St. Sampson’s Export Terminal and continued demand from construction and manufacturing sectors in the UK and mainland Europe.

“Guernsey’s metals and mining sector has demonstrated resilience and adaptability in recent years,” said industry analyst Sophie Blais. “Barring any major market shocks, the outlook for 2024 remains favorable.”
